# Records Management Training Program

## _Supporting the Development of Records and Information Management Professionals_

## Training Materials Catalog

![file folders](https://www.archives.gov/files/global-images/portal/medium/files.png)

Our [Training Materials Catalog](https://www.archives.gov/records-mgmt/training/training-catalog) contains most of the training materials that we develop, including all of the new online lessons that are part of the new training curriculum that we call Curriculum 2.0.

**The catalog includes:**

- [Online Learning](https://www.archives.gov/records-mgmt/training/online-lessons)

- [ERA 2.0 eLearning Training Materials](https://www.archives.gov/era/training)

- [Microlearning Lessons](https://www.archives.gov/records-mgmt/training/micro-lessons)

- [Videos and Webinars](https://www.archives.gov/records-mgmt/training/training-videos)

- [Job Aids](https://www.archives.gov/records-mgmt/training/job-aids)

- [Other Resources](https://www.archives.gov/records-mgmt/training/other-resources)

- [NARA Bulletins: Reformatted for Training](https://www.archives.gov/records-mgmt/training/bulletins-reformatted)

- [Legacy Training Materials (Knowledge Area Courses)](https://www.archives.gov/records-mgmt/training/list-knowledge-area-courses)

## Records Management Training

![notebook](https://www.archives.gov/files/global-images/portal/medium/notebook.png)

In 2020, the Records Management Training Program ended its in-person workshops and moved to an all-online, self-paced format.  Now, you can take our records management training on your own schedule, for free.

Our Online Learning page [Online Lessons](https://www.archives.gov/records-mgmt/training/online-lessons) gives you access to all of the training lessons we have developed.  While we no longer offer the Certificate of Federal Records Management Training, everyone can explore training content on a variety of records management topics found in our [Training Catalog](https://www.archives.gov/records-mgmt/training/training-catalog).

We are currently developing new training materials on a variety of topics.  If you would like to suggest new topics and training products, send your ideas to [rmt1@nara.gov](mailto:rmt1@nara.gov).

## Webinars

![](https://www.archives.gov/files/global-images/icons/36x36/date-time.gif)

We host webinars on records management topics that are of interest to Federal records managers.

[Recorded videos and webinars](https://www.archives.gov/records-mgmt/training/training-videos)

Please send your requests for webinars about specific topics to [rmt1@nara.gov](mailto:We host webinars on records management topics that are of interest to Federal records managers. Many of the webinars are recorded and a list is on the videos page in the training materials catalog.  Please send your requests for webinars about specific topics to%C2%A0rmt1@nara.gov.).

## Records Management Instruction Support (ReMIS)

![](https://www.archives.gov/files/global-images/icons/48x48/chalkboard.gif)

Records Management Instruction Support (ReMIS) experts provide:

- Consulting on records management training design and development
- Access to NARA records management training materials

Learn more about [ReMIS](https://www.archives.gov/records-mgmt/training/remis) and how to contact us.

​

## Agency Records Officer Credential (AROC)

![](https://www.archives.gov/files/global-images/icons/48x48/checkbox.gif)

The Agency Records Officer Credential (AROC) is required for all Senior Agency Officials for Records Management (SAORM) designated Agency Records Officers.

[More information about the certificate is available](https://www.archives.gov/records-mgmt/training/aroc).

## NARA Bulletins Formatted

![](https://www.archives.gov/files/records-mgmt/training-5.jpg)

NARA Bulletins: [Reformatted for Training](https://www.archives.gov/records-mgmt/training/bulletins-reformatted) and LMS Downloads.

Access the official [NARA Bulletins](https://www.archives.gov/records-mgmt/bulletins).

PDF files require the [free Adobe Reader.](http://www.adobe.com/reader/)

More information on Adobe Acrobat PDF files is available on our [Accessibility page](https://www.archives.gov/global-pages/accessibility/).
